Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Construction, trades & building materials · House layout, roofs, rooms & furnishings

structure noun

something built

also building, construction (a building), edifice

classical

Cic. Sen. 72: ut nāvem, ut aedificium
Varr. LL 5.141

aedificium, aedificiī n.

noun, second declension

a building, a structure

Other words

  • mōlēs, mōlis f. — a massive structure (a pier, a dam, a great pile)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Hor. C. 3.29.10: mōlem propinquam nūbibus; Caes. BC 1.25 (Lewis & Short)

  • strūctūra, strūctūrae f. — masonry, a way of building; a structure

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Caes. BC 2.9; Vitr. 5.12 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • ut nāvem, ut aedificium īdem dēstruit facillimē quī cōnstrūxit

    just as the man who built a ship or a building takes it apart most easilyCic. Sen. 72

  • vēneram in suburbānum meum et querēbar dē impēnsīs aedificiī dīlābentis

    I had come out to my place near town and was complaining about what the crumbling building was costing meSen. Ep. 12.1

See also build, build up, building site, building works, apartment building, structure.

SourcesLewis & Short: aedificium · Lewis & Short: moles · Lewis & Short: structura
